title: When Character Traits Are Out of Balance
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece challenges the assumption that more of any character strength is automatically better, arguing instead that virtues need to be balanced against complementary traits to function well. It uses responsibility and integrity as examples, showing how an unchecked strength can tip into a liability — excessive control, or rigid uncompromising behavior. The article draws on research showing character qualities are fluid rather than fixed, meaning leaders can deliberately develop underrepresented traits to restore balance. The takeaway is a more nuanced view of character than 'more virtue is always good.'
points: Character strengths aren't automatically good in unlimited amounts — they need complementary traits to stay balanced.
Unchecked responsibility can tip into over-control or reluctance to delegate.
Integrity without open-mindedness can become rigidity and inflexibility.
Research shows character qualities are fluid, not fixed, and can be deliberately developed.
The article calls for a more nuanced view of character than simply praising virtue in the abstract.
quotes: The truth is that there are very few leaders who lack any semblance of character.
The answer is Yes if the character trait is not complemented by another quality to keep it in check.
The character quality of responsibility in an extreme can encourage leaders to avoid delegating tasks to others.
The unfortunate reality is that when one character trait becomes too strong without another quality of character to create a balance with it, that virtue can become a weakness.
By consistently choosing behaviors that reflect a character quality, leaders can strengthen any aspect of their character they believe is too muted.
